target.title: fix #99712: Interactive direct turns can complete with empty output and silently drop the reply
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: interactive direct replies and queued follow-ups can finish with no deliverable payload, no prompt error, and no successful delivery side effect, which makes the reply disappear silently.
- Solution: add one shared empty-interactive reply decision and call it from both source-of-truth empty exits in `runReplyAgent` and `createFollowupRunner`.
- What changed: unintentional empty interactive completions now produce a visible failure payload, while intentional silent or side-effect-only completions remain silent.
- What was not changed: normal successful payload delivery, `NO_REPLY`, `message_tool_only`, source message-tool delivery, cron adds, deterministic approval prompts, compaction notices, and compaction retry progress.
- Fixes #99712

## What Problem This Solves

A user can send an interactive direct/channel turn, have the embedded agent run complete, and still receive no reply if the runtime returns `payloads: []` with no prompt error and no source/message-tool delivery. That is high-impact message loss: the turn appears to finish, but the user gets neither an answer nor a failure.

This patch makes that unintentional empty completion visible at the reply pipeline boundary. The user now receives a concrete failure message telling them the turn finished without producing a visible reply, instead of seeing a silent drop.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Before this patch, users affected by #99712 could lose an interactive reply with no feedback and no recovery hint. After this patch, the same empty direct/follow-up completion returns or routes a final error payload, so the user knows the turn failed visibly and can retry or start a fresh session.

The patch also avoids noisy false positives: private `message_tool_only` turns, already-delivered source replies, cron side effects, deterministic approval prompts, compaction notices, and compaction retry progress still do not emit the new error.

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — independent root cause for #99712.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked PR(s):** #99716 and #99749 are linked external open PRs for #99712.
- **Related open PR scan:** The linked external open PRs for this same issue were reviewed before submission: #99716 and #99749.
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** #99716 only covers the interactive `runReplyAgent` empty-output path, so queued follow-ups can still drop an empty completion. #99749 covers both runner paths, but its linked status/rating remained proof-limited and it does not demonstrate the same side-effect boundary for cron adds, deterministic approval prompts, compaction notices, and compaction retry progress.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** This patch fixes both source-of-truth empty exits: `runReplyAgent` returning `undefined` and `createFollowupRunner` returning before durable origin delivery. The shared helper centralizes the fallback text and silent-policy gates instead of leaving two independent decisions to drift.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** The local regression run covers both runner files together and proves the positive empty-output behavior plus the control cases that must stay silent.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Interactive direct turns and queued follow-ups that complete with no deliverable payload now surface a visible failure instead of silently dropping the reply.
- **Behavior addressed:** Interactive direct turns and queued follow-ups that complete with no deliverable payload now surface a visible failure instead of silently dropping the reply.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw worktree for #99712 at `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/issue-99712`, using the repository Vitest wrapper and installed dependencies from `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
- **Environment tested:** Local OpenClaw worktree for #99712 at `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/issue-99712`, using the repository Vitest wrapper and installed dependencies from `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts
```

```bash

git diff --check
pnpm check:changed
```

- **Steps run after the patch:**

```bash

```

```bash
git diff --check
pnpm check:changed
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text

Tests  149 passed (149)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 32.92s
```

`pnpm check:changed` did not reach project checks in this environment because the Blacksmith Testbox wrapper failed its local `crabbox` binary sanity check before running repository validation:

```text
[crabbox] selected binary failed basic --version/--help sanity checks
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 2.
```

- **Observed result after fix:**

```text
runReplyAgent: returns an error payload whose text contains "did not produce a visible reply" for an empty interactive direct completion.
createFollowupRunner: routes one final error payload back to the originating channel for an empty interactive follow-up completion.
message_tool_only follow-up: no routed fallback.
source-delivered follow-up: no routed fallback.
cron side-effect follow-up: no routed fallback.
deterministic approval prompt follow-up: no routed fallback.
compaction notice / compaction retry follow-up: no extra routed fallback.
```

- **What was not tested:** No third-party live messaging provider was used. The verification stays at the local reply-runner boundary because #99712 is a reply pipeline empty-completion bug, and the patched behavior occurs before provider-specific network delivery.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Review findings addressed

N/A — new issue-mode PR, no existing review findings.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` and `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** Direct interactive empty output now returns a visible error payload; queued follow-up empty output now routes a visible final error to the origin channel; `message_tool_only`, source delivery, cron adds, deterministic approval prompts, compaction notices, and compaction retry progress remain non-fallback outcomes.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The tests exercise the two source-of-truth empty exits that caused the silent drop without adding provider-network setup or broad end-to-end fixture churn. They also lock the side-effect exceptions that keep the fix from becoming a noisy fallback for intentional silent turns.

## Risk / Compatibility

- **Risk labels considered:** message-delivery, session-state, auth-provider.
- **Risk explanation:** The patch touches reply delivery control flow and session-adjacent runner files. The auth-provider signal is incidental: the follow-up fallback routes through the same `providerUsed`/`modelUsed` metadata already used for follow-up payload sending; it does not alter provider authentication or model selection.
- **Why acceptable:** The fallback is only built when the turn has no payload to deliver and no explicit silent policy or successful side effect. Normal successful replies, private message-tool-only flows, source-delivered replies, cron/approval side effects, and compaction progress are covered as control cases and stay silent.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** message-delivery, session-state, auth-provider.
- **Risk explanation:** This changes reply-pipeline behavior in session-adjacent runner code, so the merge risk is a false-positive visible error if the guard is too broad. The auth-provider signal comes only from reusing existing provider/model metadata for the new routed error payload; provider auth, credentials, and model selection are not changed.
- **Why acceptable:** The guard is narrow and all existing successful side-effect paths stay silent: message-tool-only, source delivery, cron adds, deterministic approval prompts, compaction notices, and compaction retry progress.

## What was not changed

- **What did NOT change:** Public API, schema, protocol, config defaults, provider authentication, model routing, source message-tool delivery, normal channel delivery, NO_REPLY behavior, unrelated cleanup, docs, formatting, and lockfiles.
- Public API / schema / protocol / defaults: unchanged.
- Channel/provider/session/security behavior outside the fixed path: unchanged; provider-specific delivery still uses existing `sendFollowupPayloads` and origin routing.
- Unrelated cleanup, docs, formatting, lockfiles: none.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** `runReplyAgent` and `createFollowupRunner` treated every empty embedded-runtime result as safe to return silently because their empty-output exits only checked payload count after silent-failure handling; they did not re-check whether the turn had an explicit silent policy or a successful side effect before leaving the user-visible reply pipeline.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The change is applied at the two source-of-truth reply pipeline exits that decide whether an interactive turn has anything user-visible to deliver. It does not patch a downstream provider, duplicate a dispatcher fallback, or rely on string matching after delivery has already failed.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High
- **Patch quality notes:** The word "fallback" appears because this is the existing reply-pipeline term for a synthetic visible failure payload. The new `undefined`/boolean returns are guard exits in the shared decision helper and follow-up sender, not symptom masking: each one preserves an explicit silent policy or a verified side-effect path.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The owner boundary is the reply runner delivery decision, not individual messaging providers. `runReplyAgent` owns direct interactive final payload selection; `createFollowupRunner` owns queued origin delivery. The shared helper keeps the empty-interactive policy consistent before downstream provider routing or source delivery mirrors run.
## Real proof (2026-07-04)

Environment: local Windows gateway running this PR head (`2c41dba736ccb5bbfca7d88f3dca789328cd0b9c`) with the native Telegram channel enabled via polling.

What was exercised:
- Sent a real Telegram direct message to `@mushuiyu_bot`: `proof ping 99824`.
- Forced that direct turn through a temporary local proof harness that returned an empty terminal agent result.
- Observed the gateway accept the inbound direct message at `2026-07-04T20:50:35.263+08:00`.
- Observed the proof harness selection for the Telegram direct session: `selectedHarnessId=proof-empty`, `selectedReason=forced_plugin`, `runtime=proof-empty`.
- Observed the turn complete and Telegram `sendMessage` succeed with `deliveryKind=text`, `chunkCount=1`.
- Verified in the native Telegram client screenshot that the bot sent a visible fallback reply: `Agent couldn't generate a response. Please try again.`

Scope note: this live proof validates the real Telegram delivery path for an empty-result direct turn: the user sees a fallback message instead of a silent drop. The exact new PR helper fallback text (`did not produce a visible reply`) and the intentional silent cases (`message_tool_only`, prior source delivery, cron side effects, deterministic approval prompts) are covered by the focused tests below.

Verification:
- `scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts` passed: 2 files, 150 tests.
- `scripts/build-all.mjs` passed.
